provenance.l: NSSDCA Viking 1 Lander (Viking Lander EDL — Soffen & Snyder 1976) — entry 4.5 km/s at −17.6° (relative), 930 kg, β 63.7 kg/m²; chute at ~6 km, terminal engines from ~1.5 km, touchdown 2.4 m/s. Entry-interface altitude not found in the sources read

Viking EDL as researched for pass 2 (docs/wip/2026-11-23-mars-landings-record.md): 3.5 m aeroshell; a single disk-gap-band chute (16 m, the record marks it unverified) at about 5.5–6 km; the aeroshell off 8–14 s later (10 s drawn); three throttled engines of 18 nozzles each lit at about 1.5 km with the chute and backshell released; a constant-velocity descent from 17 m at 2.4 m/s (the record also gives 1.5 m/s and about 2 m/s on three legs; 2.4 m/s is the figure the profile and the brief use). The leg deploy (5 s after the aeroshell) and the radar lock (1.7 km) are drawn, not sourced
